result:
None of the three final answers matches the value I recall, which is α = 2. I could not derive this from scratch, and it rests on my memory of a result on tree decompositions with small spread.

My recollection is that every graph has a tree decomposition of width at most about 2·tw(G)+1 in which each vertex v lies in O(d(v)+1) bags, and that no constant c < 2 can achieve this. If so, P(c) is impossible exactly for c < 2, giving α = 2.

**Solution 1** claims α = ∞. Its cycle argument is wrong: cycles have a tree decomposition of width 2 in which every vertex is in O(1) bags, so the claimed Ω(log n) spread lower bound does not hold. Reject.

**Solution 2** claims α = 1. It argues that P(1) fails and P(c) holds for all c > 1, but the construction for c > 1 is only hand-waved. It also conflicts with the known threshold of 2. Reject.

**Solution 3** claims α = 3. It cites "IMC 2011 Problem 10" as a source and gives no real derivation, so I do not trust it. The value also does not match 2. Reject.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
